newsitem.title: GERMANY: Online ratings divides German media industry.
newsitem.headline: Online ratings divides German media industry.

text.p: A leading German publishing company on Friday distanced itself from marketing agency MediaGruppe Muenchen (MGM) in the latest battle over a standard online ratings system.

A spokesman from publisher Spiegel-Verlag said it would postpone planned research projects on new media marketing with MGM due to disagreements about finding an accurate rating system in the still infant business of Internet advertising.

MGM recently announced it planned to measure popularity with users with a system called AdClicks, which counts the number of mouse clicks on an advertiser's icon and breaks with a newly developed media industry standard.
"We are of the opinion that with the new industry standard, the performance of an online advertisement is sufficiently measured," said Spiegel spokesman Kurt Otto.
Spiegel worked feverishly in recent months with media industry associations on developing what they hoped would emerge as the industry benchmark for online ratings.

This system counts contacts with entire web pages and sites, called Page Views and Visits, which defenders say distinguishes between users who are interested in an entire site and those who only click on the advertisements.

"Our investors have big reservations about AdClicks," Otto said, "because it does not measure the performance of the media carrying the advertisements but just the content and attractiveness of the ads."
